$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) & =2(4)+1=9 \\ g(4) & =-3(4)+5=-7\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we add the results:

$$
(f+g)(4)=f(4)+g(4)=9+(-7)=2
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(f+g)(x) & =(2x+1)+(-3x+5) \\  & =-x+6 \\  & =6-x\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(f+g)(4) & =6-4=2\end{aligned}

**Method 1**

To evaluate $(f/g)(3),$ we find $f(3)$ and $g(3),$ and then divide the results.

First, we find $f(3)$ and $g(3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3) & =2(3)^{2}-6=12 \\ g(3) & =-2(3)+2=-4\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we divide the results:

$$
(f/g)(3)=\frac{f(3)}{g(3)}=\frac{12}{-4}=-3
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(f/g)(x)=\frac{2{x}^{2}-6}{-2x+2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

\end{aligned}

\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate $(f + g)(1)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
(f + g)(1) &= (1)^{2} + 2(1) - 4 =-1
\end{aligned}
$$

Both these methods work fine, but method $1$ is usually faster.
